## Data handling & curation

Managing the "data life-cycle" within and beyond a project.

-   creating data
-   organising data
-   maintaining data

## Data cleaning vs Data wrangling

***Data cleaning*** is the process of removing incorrect, duplicate, or otherwise erroneous data from a dataset

***Data wrangling*** changing the format to make it more useful for your analysis

## Clean your data with code

Why? What could go wrong?

## Avoiding name conflicts

```{r}
#| label: penguins-tibble
#| echo: false
penguins <- as_tibble(penguins)
```


```{r}
#| label: conflicts
#| output-location: fragment
#| message: false
#| error: true
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)

penguins |> select(species, body_mass)
```

::: fragment
### Explictly name packages

```{r}
penguins |> dplyr::select(species, body_mass)
```
:::

## Conflicted

Turns namespace conflicts into errors

```{r}
#| error: true
library(conflicted)
penguins |> select(species, body_mass)
```


::: fragment
Prefer functions from a particular package. 

```{r}
conflict_prefer_all("dplyr", quiet = TRUE)
penguins |> select(species, body_mass)
```
:::

# Missing data

## Missing data

Missing data is normally a problem. Typically as ecologists we sweep missing data under the carpet by using a "complete case" approach to data analysis.

![](images/SWEEP-IT-UNDER-THE-CARPET-BANKSY-2.jpg)

## Visualising missing data

### {naniar}

```{r}
# creating some data with missing values
missing_penguins <- missMethods::delete_MCAR(clean_penguins, 0.3)


missing_penguins |>
  naniar::vis_miss()
```

## 

If you have ever written some code like this:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# na.omit()
df <- na.omit(df)
# complete.cases()
df <- df[complete.cases(df), ]
# rowSums()
df <- df[rowSums(is.na(df)) == 0, ]
# drop_na()
df <- df |> tidyr::drop_na()
```

you are removing missing data (NAs) from your dataset.

## Why is this a problem?

By throwing away potentially useful data (only including those rows without a NA in them) you

- reduce the information you are working with
- reduce statistical power
- introduce selection bias (invalidating any assumption of randomisation).

## Different types of missingness

There are three broad categories of missing data:

-   MCAR - missingness is not related to any measured or unmeasured variables

-   MAR - missingness is not random but related to other variables and can be accounted for by another complete variable

-   MNAR - missingness is related to the missing data itself (there is a systematic reason why the data are missing within a particular variable)

## The effect of missingness

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(missMethods)

# create datasets with levels missingness

penguins_complete <- penguins |>
  drop_na()

miss_penguins_MCAR <- delete_MCAR(
    penguins_complete,
    0.3, "flipper_len"
  )
# create a pattern of missingness with censoring
# (missing value in flipper_length if body_mass in below 30% quantile)

miss_penguins_MAR <- delete_MAR_censoring(
    penguins_complete,
    0.3, "flipper_len", "body_mass"
  )
# create a pattern of missingness with censoring
# (missing value in flipper_length if flipper_length is below 30% quantile)

miss_penguins_MNAR <- delete_MNAR_censoring(
    penguins_complete,
    0.3, "flipper_len"
  )

all_data <- bind_rows(
  "Full" = penguins_complete,
  "MCAR" = miss_penguins_MCAR,
  "MAR" = miss_penguins_MAR,
  "MNAR" = miss_penguins_MNAR,
  .id = "Missingness"
)
```

## 

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# plot the missing data function

MDplot <- function(df_comp, df_mis, title) {
  df_comp$missX <- is.na(df_mis$flipper_len)
  ggplot(data = df_comp, aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, colour = missX)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    labs(x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Body mass (g)") +
    scale_color_discrete(name = "Missing data?") +
    ggtitle(title)
  #+ theme_bw()
}
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
MDplot(penguins_complete, miss_penguins_MCAR, title = "MCAR")
```

## 

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
MDplot(penguins_complete, miss_penguins_MAR, title = "MAR")
```

## 

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
MDplot(penguins_complete, miss_penguins_MNAR, title = "MNAR")
```

## What to do about missing data?

With MCAR and MAR we can use multiple imputation techniques

![](images/MICE.png)

## 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| label: mice-setup
# Load mice
library(mice)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Simulate data: location, year, count 
data <- data.frame(              # Create a dataframe
  Location = rep(1:5, each = 5), # Assuming 5 locations, 
  Year = rep(2009:2023, 5),      # Assuming data for 5 years, 
  Count = rpois(25, lambda = 20) # Simulated count data
)  

# Introduce missingness - Missing completely at random (MCAR)
prop_missing <- 0.2 # Example: 20% missingness
missing_indices <- sample(1:nrow(data), prop_missing * nrow(data))
data$Count[missing_indices] <- NA
```

## 

When we impute the missing data we use 5 replicates and then take the mean of all 5 datasets.

```{r}
#| label: mice
#| output: false
# Impute missing data using MICE
imp <- mice(data, m = 5, method = "pmm", seed = 500)
```

## 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Analyse trends and variation in the original and imputed data
# For illustration purposes, assuming a simple trend analysis
original_trend <- aggregate(data$Count, by = list(data$Year), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
names(original_trend) <- c("Year", "Count")
imputed_trend <- complete(imp, "long")
imputed_trend <- aggregate(Count ~ Year, data = imputed_trend, FUN = mean)

# Visualization of trends in original and imputed data
plot_data <- bind_rows("original" = original_trend, "imputed" = imputed_trend, .id = "Trend")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
plot_data |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, Count, colour = Trend)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```

## sem() instead of lm()

Using a Structured Equation Model (SEM) we can run a simple linear regression.

```{r, echo=TRUE,message=FALSE}
library(lavaan)
# we will use the Iris dataset for this example
complete_model <- lm(Petal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length, data = iris)

iris_MCAR <- missMethods::delete_MCAR(iris, 0.3, "Sepal.Width")

miss_model1 <- lm(Petal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length, data = iris_MCAR)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(stargazer, quietly = TRUE)
stargazer(complete_model, miss_model1,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
  no.space = T, type = "text"
)
```

## 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
miss_model2 <- sem(
  model = "Petal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length", 
  data = iris_MCAR,
  missing = "ML")
summary(miss_model2)
```

The argument `missing = "ML"` to the `sem()` function estimates a likelihood function for each row based on the variables that are present.

Let all the available data be used.

## Data validation

```{r}
library(data.validator)
report <- data_validation_report()

between <- function(a, b) {
  function(x) {
    a <= x & x <= b
  }
}

validate(iris, name = "Verifying flower dataset") |>
  validate_if(
    expr = Sepal.Length > 0, 
    description = "Sepal length is greater than 0"
  ) |>
  validate_cols(
    predicate = between(0, 4), 
    Sepal.Width, 
    description = "Sepal width is between 0 and 4"
  ) |>
  add_results(report)

print(report)
```

## 

```{r}
print(report)
```

## Transform to long format

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

penguins_long <- palmerpenguins::penguins |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = contains("_"), 
    names_to = c("part", "measure", "unit"), 
    names_sep = "_"
  )

penguins_long
```

## Transform to wide format

```{r}
penguins_long |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = value)
```

## What's going on?

No identifier for each observation so R puts all the values in a list. To solve this we need a unique row id.

```{r}
penguins_long |>
  mutate(sample = row_number()) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = value)
```

## Separate

One cell should contain one thing

```{r}
#| label: separate
df <- tibble(id = 1:3, x = c("m-123", "f-455", "f-123"))
df

# separate into columns by delimiter
df |> separate_wider_delim(x, delim = "-", names = c("sex", "unit"))
```

# Style

## Code is communication

-   With your computer

-   With your collaborators

> "Your closest collaborator is you six months ago but you don't reply to email."
> --- Paul Wilson

-   With reviewers/examiners

Need understandable code

["Good coding style is like correct punctuation: you can manage without it, butitsuremakesthingseasiertoread."](https://style.tidyverse.org/)

## Journal code archiving requirements {.scrollable}

### [Nature Journals](https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards)

> A condition of publication in a Nature Portfolio journal is that authors are required to make materials, data, **code**, and associated protocols promptly available to readers without undue qualifications.

### [Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences](https://blog.cdnsciencepub.com/open-data-and-code-in-fisheries-and-aquatic-science/)

>  it is a condition for publication of accepted manuscripts at CJFAS that authors make publicly available all data and **code** needed to reproduce those results (including code to reproduce statistical results, simulation results, and figures) via an online data repository.

## Naming Things

> "There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things."

> --- Phil Karlton

-   Names can contain letters, numbers, "\_" and "."
-   Names must begin with a letter or "."
-   Avoid using names of existing functions - confusing
-   Make names concise yet meaningful
-   Reserved words include `TRUE`, `for`, `if`

## Naming convensions

| camelCase 🐫      | UpperCamelCase    | snake_case 🐍       |
|-------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| billLengthMM      | BillLengthMM      | bill_length_mm      |
| bergenWeather2022 | BergenWeather2022 | bergen_weather_2022 |
| dryMassG          | DryMassG          | dry_mass_g          |
| makeWeatherPlot   | MakeWeatherPlot   | make_weather_plot   |

## White-space is free!

Place spaces

-   around infix operators (`|>`, `+`, `-`, `<-`, )
-   around `=` in function calls
-   after commas not before

### Good

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gentoo <- filter(penguins, species == "Gentoo", body_mass_g >= 300)
```

### Bad

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gentoo<-filter(penguins,species=="Gentoo",body_mass_g>=300)
```

## Split long commands over multiple lines

### Bad

```{r, eval = FALSE}
penguins |> group_by(species) |> summarise(max_mass = max(body_mass_g), mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm), .groups = "drop")
```

### Good

```{r, eval = FALSE}
penguins |> 
  group_by(species) |> 
  summarise(
    max_mass = max(body_mass_g),
    mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm),
   .groups = "drop"
  )
```

::: notes
Aim for a maximum line length of 80 characters
:::

## Indentation makes code readable

### Good

```{r, eval = FALSE}
positive <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(dim(x))) {
    x[x > 0]
  } else{
    x[, colSums(x) > 0, drop  = FALSE]
  }
}
```

### Bad

```{r, eval = FALSE}
positive <- function(x){
if(is.null(dim(x)))
{x[x >0]} 
else{
x[, colSums(x) > 0, drop  = FALSE]
}}
```


## Comments

Use \# to start comments.

Help you and others to understand what you did

Comments should explain the why, not the what.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Bad
# remove line 37 of the penguins dataset
penguins <- penguins[-37, ]
```


Try to make code self-documenting with descriptive object names

## Comments for navigation

Helps you find your way around a script

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#### Load data ####
...

#### Plot data ####
...
```

## No magic numbers

```{r}
# Bad
x <- c(1, 5, 6, 3, 6)
mean(x)
x[x > 4.2]
```
::: fragment
```{r}
# Good
x <- c(1, 5, 6, 3, 6)
x_mean <- mean(x)
x[x > x_mean]
```
:::


## Don't repeat yourself

Repeated code is hard to maintain

Make repeated code into functions.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
my_fun <- function(arg1) {arg1 ^ 2}
my_fun(7)
```

Single place to maintain

## Split analyses over multiple files

Long scripts become difficult to navigate

Fix by moving parts of the code into different files

For example:

-   data import code to "loadData.R"
-   functions to "functions.R"

Import with

```{r, eval = FALSE}
source("1-functions.R")
source("2-loadData.R")
```

Number files so they sort alphabetically in order of use.



## Organising a project

All in one directory - messy

```{r}
#| echo: false
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "bad")
fs::dir_create(d)
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "thesis.Rproj"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "data1.csv"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "data2.csv"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "introduction.qmd"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "discussion.qmd"))

fs::dir_tree(d)
```

Directories for each type of file - clean

```{r}
#| echo: false
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "good")
fs::dir_create(d)
fs::dir_create(file.path(d, "data"))
fs::dir_create(file.path(d, "chapters"))

fs::file_create(file.path(d, "thesis.Rproj"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "data", "data1.csv"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "data", "data2.csv"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "chapters", "1-introduction.qmd"))
fs::file_create(file.path(d, "chapters", "2-discussion.qmd"))

fs::dir_tree(d)
```

## Useful packages for style

Some badly formatted code in "bad_style.R"

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Define the code as a character vector
code <- c(
  "# Spacing ",
  "average<-mean(feet/12 + inches,na.rm=TRUE)",
  "sqrt(x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)",
  "x <- 1 : 10",
  "base :: get",
  "# Indenting",
  "if (y < 0 && debug)",
  "message('Y is negative')",
  "# Assignment",
  "x = 5"
)

# Write the code to 'bad_style.R'
writeLines(code, "bad_style.R")
paste(code, collapse = "\n") |> cat()
```

## `lintr` for static code analysis

Detects style issues, syntax errors and fragile code 

```{r}
#| label: lintr
# Run lintr on the newly created file
library(lintr)
lint("bad_style.R") # usually run from RStudio Addins
```

## `styler` to fix your style

```{r}
#| label: styler
library("styler")
style_file("bad_style.R") # usually run from RStudio Addins
```


```{r}

```
